sections.heading: How to Play Marksmanship
sections.body:
[h2 type=bar toc="How to Play Marksmanship"][color=c3]Marksmanship Hunter Rotation in Midnight Season 2[/color][/h2]

The rotation for Marksmanship Hunter focuses on maximizing your use of certain buffs, and maximizing your number of uses of cooldown-limited abilities. Marksmanship has a fairly consistent flow, where one ability logically flows into the next, with a few priority shifts based on procs and buff uptimes.

[wrapper width=1100px][box border=true]
[center][table style=grid]
[tr][td]
[table]
[tr]
[td width=6%][icon name=ability_hunter_snipertraining size=medium type=round color=c3 inline=true][/icon][/td]
[td][b][color=c3][spell=260240]:[/color][/b] These procs are guaranteed to happen from all [spell=19434]s, and, depending on Talents, [spell=257044] as well. They are spent on [spell=185358] on single-target and [spell=257620] on 2+ targets, at least when we play [spell=257621]. Every single proc must be spent, which in practice means following up every [spell=19434] with an [spell=185358] or [spell=257620]. [spell=257044] spends its own proc, because [spell=1277548] fires an [spell=185358] as it starts and finishes.
[/td][/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
[tr]
[td width=6%][icon name=ability_hunter_runningshot size=medium type=round color=c3 inline=true][/icon][/td]
[td][b][color=c3]Always Be Casting:[/color][/b] Casting as many abilities as possible matters more than pressing the perfect button every time, and dead time is the single biggest thing holding most players back from their DPS goals. [spell=56641] is how you fill it, and it is castable while moving, so there is no excuse for a dead global. The best Marksmanship Hunters will have way more [spell=56641] casts than someone more average, in large part because they do not ever stop casting when moving or dealing with mechanics.
[/td][/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
[tr]
[td width=6%][icon name=ability_druid_dash size=medium type=round color=c3 inline=true][/icon][/td]
[td][b][color=c3]Movement:[/color][/b] While not strictly a rotational concept, while the flow of Marksmanship is straightforward, managing your movement is a big part of mastering it. The core thing to remember is that you should try and reserve movement for when you are not casting [spell=19434]. Whenever you are not casting [spell=19434], you can move freely without interrupting your rotation, and you should take advantage of this fact to always think "can I be positioned ever so slightly better" and to move accordingly. Standing still while not casting [spell=19434] is rarely the best move.[/td]
[/tr]
[/table]
[/td][/tr][/table]
[/center]
[/box][/wrapper]
[pad]

sections.heading: Rotation Priority
sections.body:
[h2 type=bar toc="Rotation Priority"][icon name=ability_hunter_focusedaim type=round size=medium inline=true color=c3][/icon] Best Marksmanship Hunter Rotation[/h2]

Our rotation has a fairly simple priority structure, with a few nuances based on procs and buffs. There is a fairly consistent flow to the rotation, where one button leads into the next, and there are not many decisions to make outside of "do I have this proc or buff".

Below, we break down the main priority lists for Marksmanship Hunter: Single-Target Rotation, AoE Rotation, and your opener sequence.
[wrapper width=70%][center][box border=true]
[center][large][b][color=white]Hero Talent Master Switches[/color][/b][/large]
[pad]
You can use the master switches below to flip the [b][i]entire page's[/i][/b] options to your selected choice.[/center]

[center]
[wrapper width=95%]
[grid column-width=49%]
[display-option="sentinel" radio="Hero" icon=inv_ability_sentinelhunter_lunarstorm checked]Sentinel[/display-option]
[display-option="darkranger" radio="Hero" icon=inv_ability_darkrangerhunter_blackarrow]Dark Ranger[/display-option]
[/grid]
[/wrapper]
[/center]
[/box][/center][/wrapper]
[br]
[tabs name="Rotations" uniform=true]

[tab name="Single-Target Priority" icon=spell_holy_divinespirit]
[h3 toc="Single Target Priority" type=bar][color=c3] Best Marksmanship Hunter Single Target Rotation[/color][/h3]
[pad]

Below is the priority system that describes the optimal single-target rotation for Marksmanship Hunter.

The core loop of Marksmanship is to cast [spell=19434] and [spell=257044] on cooldown. These will both activate [spell=260240], which buffs [spell=185358]/[spell=53351]/[spell=466932] ([symbol=wow-hero-talent-dark-ranger] [color=purple-gem]Dark Ranger[/color]) significantly. Every [spell=19434] should thus be followed up by a "PS Spender" like this. We usually run the [spell=1277548] talent, which actually causes [spell=257044] to consume the [spell=260240] proc that it generates by itself. So, [spell=19434] on cooldown, follow them up with a PS Spender, and [spell=257044] on cooldown. On top of this, we add [spell=212431] and [spell=260243] on cooldown. [spell=56641] is your filler when you can do absolutely nothing else.

[pad]

[li]Cast [spell=466932] if you have [spell=260240].[/li]

[h3 toc="AoE Priority" type=bar][color=c3] Best Marksmanship Hunter AoE  Rotation[/color][/h3]
[pad]

The primary change for AoE is simply replacing [spell=185358] with [spell=257620], at least while we run [spell=257621] Talent, which we do not always do. While [spell=257621] is a core and crucial mechanic when we run the talent, it actually takes care of itself, because it is generated from [spell=257620], a button that we already press to spend our [spell=260240] procs. It is essential that we never cast [spell=19434] or [spell=257044] without the [spell=257621] buff, but by just following the same principles as our single-target rotation of always following up all of our [spell=19434]s with a [spell=257620], we will always have [spell=257621] uptime without needing to think about it at all. The only exception here is that all [spell=257044]s must be followed up with a [spell=257620], and you should cast that [spell=257620] just before the channel finishes so that you clip the last tick.

Use a [url=https://azortharion.com/multimacro]mouseover Multi-Shot macro[/url] to cast [spell=257620] at a different target.

Without [spell=257621], which is to say when running [spell=470945], the AoE rotation is [b]almost identical to the Single-Target rotation[/b]. Refer to the Sentinel Single-Target Priority above and follow it. The one change is that [spell=257620] replaces [spell=185358] as your [spell=260240] spender once two or more enemies are up, unless you are deliberately focusing a priority target.

[h2 toc=false type=bar]Pre-Combat Check[/h2]
Before any combat happens, it is important for Marksmanship Hunter to make sure the following are done. This applies to raids, dungeons, delves, or even open-world content.
[center][wrapper width=800px][center][box]
[ul]
[li icon=exclamation-circle]Drink [item=241326].[/li]
[li icon=exclamation-circle]Apply [item=243734].[/li]
[li icon=exclamation-circle]Pre-pot with [item=241288] just before the pull.[/li]
[li icon=exclamation-circle]Carry a [item=271887] for your second Potion later in the fight.[/li]
[li icon=exclamation-circle]Apply [item=259085].[/li]
[li icon=exclamation-circle]Apply [spell=257284] to your target. If there are multiple Hunters, coordinate which ones you each Mark.[/li]
[li icon=exclamation-circle]Eat [item=266985]. The Hearty variety is worth the extra cost because it does not fade when you die.[/li]
[/ul]
[/box][/center][/wrapper][/center]

sections.heading: Major Cooldowns
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Major Cooldowns" type=bar][color=c3][icon name=ability_hunter_focusedaim type=round size=medium inline=true color=c3][/icon] Marksmanship Hunter Major Cooldowns[/color][/h2]

Marksmanship only has one cooldown of note, [spell=288613]. It has almost no impact on our rotation, with most of its value being in its crit chance and crit damage buff. It does also speed up our [spell=19434] and [spell=257044] cooldowns, but this does not impact our rotational priorities, and is more of a "nice to have" rather than something that we build our rotation around.
[pad]
[tabs name="cds" uniform=true iconborders=true]

[tab name="Trueshot" icon=ability_trueshot]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=hunter] Trueshot [/color][/h3]

[spell=288613] massively increases our critical strike chance, damage, and the cooldown rates of [spell=19434] and [spell=257044], as well as [spell=19434]'s cast time. It makes us do everything stronger and faster.

Our rotational priorities barely change inside [spell=288613]. The handful that do are in the priority lists above.

For [symbol=wow-hero-talent-dark-ranger] [color=purple-gem]Dark Ranger[/color], activating Trueshot also gives us a [spell=466932] proc, which we need to activate [spell=260240] before we can fire.

For both Hero Talents, activating [spell=288613] turns the Trueshot button into another ability: [spell=1264902] for [symbol=wow-hero-talent-sentinel] [color=exalted]Sentinel[/color], and [spell=392060] for [symbol=wow-hero-talent-dark-ranger] [color=purple-gem]Dark Ranger[/color]. Each one is a single cast, so use it where it will not push back your other priorities. For [symbol=wow-hero-talent-sentinel] [color=exalted]Sentinel[/color] on single target that means firing [spell=1264902] with roughly 5 seconds of [spell=288613] left.
[/tab]
[/tabs]

sections.heading: Advanced Tips
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Advanced Tips" type=bar][color=c3][icon name=Inv_artifact_tome01 type=round size=medium inline=true color=c3][/icon] Marksmanship Hunter Advanced Tips[/color][/h2]

You could argue that it is a basic tip, but it is still the #1 issue that even "good" Marksmanship Hunters face, and it is to ensure that you are [b]always[/b] casting something. Marksmanship always has something to cast, because even if you run out of absolutely every resource and cooldown, you can always [spell=56641], and within 2 seconds, you are back to casting [spell=19434].
[pad]
[tabs name="advanced" uniform=true iconborders=true]
[tab name="Always Be Casting" icon=ability_hunter_runningshot]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c3] Always Be Casting [/color][/h3]
The problem is not so much that people forget that [spell=56641] exists, however. It is understanding the value of [b]time[/b] in the DPS equation. Most people press their buttons rather slowly, they press buttons that are not available to them, their DPS rotation stops when they are focused on a mechanic, or they just have bad reaction times. All of these things lead to lost time where you are not casting anything, often for very small windows of time, but these small windows of time add up very quickly, and they are the difference between a good and a great player. Always be casting something, even if it is just [spell=56641], and you will see a noticeable increase in your DPS.
[/tab]
[/tabs]
[pad]

Our Marksmanship Hunter guides are always updated with the latest information from in-game experience, simulations, and logs. Make sure to check our changelog for this page by clicking on [b]View Changelog[/b] in the Quick Facts column or on the book icon at the top of the page. If you are interested in more in-depth Marksmanship Hunter guides for [b]Midnight Season 2[/b], make sure to browse the [i]Navigation Bar[/i] at the top of the page, along with our list of [b]Related Guides[/b] just beneath the [i]Table of Contents[/i].

[tooltip name=Aimed2ChargeRF][color=q]With Aimed Shot having 2 charges, we are fine to leave it unused at 1 charge since its cooldown is still regenerating. What we don't want is for it to ever reach 2 charges, because then its cooldown is not ticking. This is why we are happy to prioritize Rapid Fire over it when it only has 1 charge, but not two.[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=RFClipSentinel][color=q]You'll press [spell=257620] after [spell=257044] in almost every case, so press it just before the channel ends and you will only lose the final tick. That [spell=257620] should be targeted on a different target, potentially spreading [spell=1253601] to that target, which is worth considerably more than the lost RF tick.[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=RFPreciseSentinelST][color=q]A single [spell=260240] can get spent twice here. [spell=1277548] adds a shot at each end of the channel: the first takes the proc you had going in, then [spell=473385] replaces it, and the last Unload shot consumes the replacement.[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=OBR_with][color=q]Utilizing your cooldowns as they become available, timing them with other cooldowns, and overlapping properly.[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=OBR_without][color=q]Following the Assisted Combat suggestions exactly, or only pressing the Single-Button without any other buttons being used.[/color][/tooltip]
